Let <MATH_0001> be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes.
Let <MATH_0002> be a quasi-coherent sheaf on <MATH_0003>. For either the <ACCENT_0001>tale
or Zariski topology, there are canonical isomorphisms
<MATH_0004>.

We prove this for the <ACCENT_0001>tale topology; we omit the proof in the case
of the Zariski topology. By Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma
<REF_0001>
the sheaves <MATH_0001> are quasi-coherent so that the assertion
makes sense. The sheaf <MATH_0002> is the sheaf associated
to the presheaf
<MATH_0003>
where <MATH_0004> is an object of <MATH_0005>, see
Cohomology on Sites, Lemma <REF_0002>.
By our conventions the right hand side is the <ACCENT_0002>tale
cohomology of the restriction of <MATH_0006> to the localization
<MATH_0007> which equals
<MATH_0008>. By
Proposition <REF_0003>
this is presheaf the same as the presheaf
<MATH_0009>
where <MATH_0010> is the projection. If <MATH_0011> is affine
then this is the same as <MATH_0012>, see
Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma
<REF_0004>.
By
Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma <REF_0005>
this is equal to <MATH_0013> which is the value
of <MATH_0014> on <MATH_0015>.
Thus the values of the sheaves of modules
<MATH_0016> and <MATH_0017>
on every affine object of <MATH_0018> are canonically isomorphic
which implies they are canonically isomorphic.
